name: fsetxattr
synopsis: int fsetxattr(int fd, const char *name, const void *value, size_t size, int flags);
description: fsetxattr() sets the value of an extended attribute for an open file descriptor. It associates a name:value pair with the file, allowing for creation or replacement based on specified flags.

parameters.name: fd
parameters.description: File descriptor of the open file on which to set the extended attribute.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Null-terminated string specifying the name of the extended attribute, including a namespace prefix.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Pointer to the value to be set for the extended attribute.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Size in bytes of the value pointed to by value; can be zero for an empty value.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags to control behavior, such as XATTR_CREATE (fail if attribute exists) or XATTR_REPLACE (fail if attribute does not exist).

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: Disk quota limits prevent storing the extended attribute.
XATTR_CREATE was specified, but the attribute already exists.
XATTR_REPLACE was specified, but the attribute does not exist.
Insufficient space to store the extended attribute.
Extended attributes are not supported by the filesystem, disabled, or the namespace prefix is invalid.
The file is marked immutable or append-only.
The size of name or value exceeds a filesystem-specific limit.
